planner_ruling_sentinel.question: The design doc specified a sentinel-panic abort on drain-budget exhaustion, recovered around ctx.AI.StepWithStream. The controller refuted it as unsound on js && wasm. Options: (i) no sentinel, (ii) native-only gated sentinel, (iii) keep as designed.
planner_ruling_sentinel.ruling: (i) - drain mode ships, the sentinel does NOT. Controller refutation CONFIRMED and strengthened against a primary source.
reasons: R1: Go 1.26.5 syscall/js FuncOf doc: 'Invoking the wrapped Go function from JavaScript will pause the event loop and spawn a new goroutine. Other wrapped functions which are triggered during a call from Go to JavaScript get executed on the same goroutine.' WasmAIHandler.StepWithStream returns from Invoke with a thenable and parks in awaitPromise's select (cmd/wasm/effects.go:53-88), so every later funcWrapper call arrives from the JS event loop on a NEW goroutine. recover is per-goroutine => unrecovered => fatal to the module.

R2: option (iii) refuted - it needs the JS handler to emit synchronously inside Invoke, but the repo's own StepWithStream comment says the wrapper is released 'once the JS handler resolves its Promise', and any real streaming handler is async. A soundness property a third-party caller can revoke is not a soundness property.

R3: option (ii) refuted - (a) PR CI never compiles js && wasm (grep -n wasm .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/build.yml => rc=1 zero hits; control: 20+ hits in release.yml, build-wasm job at :17), so a build-tag slip surfaces at RELEASE not on the PR; (b) on WASM the drain branch is unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION - jsToStreamChunk (cmd/wasm/effects.go:345-366) returns only the 3 encodable variants or untyped nil, and :243 filters nil before onChunk - so the gated sentinel is dead code today, and the only scenario that activates it (a 4th variant added to jsToStreamChunk without an encodeStreamChunk case) is exactly where a wrong gate turns 'typed Internal + long drain' into 'fatal WASM module crash'.

R4: the sentinel is a covert version of the interface change Mark already rejected. AIHandler.StepWithStream has 7 implementers (4 production, 3 test doubles) PLUS out-of-repo ones including @arniwesth's driver. Panicking out of the onChunk we hand them imposes an unstated panic-transparency requirement with no compiler signal, no interface doc, no version bump. Mark rejected option (b) because an interface change reaching WASM forfeits the purely-additive property; the sentinel forfeits it invisibly.
planner_ruling_sentinel.doc_argument_refuted: The doc claimed the sentinel is 'the established Go control-flow escape ... (encoding/json, fmt use it internally)'. encoding/json's only recover is encode.go:335 in (*encodeState).marshal, and the jsonError it catches is raised by json's OWN encodeState recursion; a panic from a user-supplied MarshalJSON is explicitly RE-RAISED at encode.go:339. The precedent is 'a package panics through its own frames', never 'a package panics out of a callback it handed to foreign code'.
planner_ruling_sentinel.what_survives: drain mode, both named budgets, drain_exhausted trace metadata, the preserved typed Internal error, locality, no interface change - every element of Mark's option-(c) ruling.
planner_ruling_sentinel.residual_for_human: Post-failure WALL-CLOCK is no longer bounded; only post-failure WORK is. On a path unreachable for any StreamChunk constructible today. One-word question to Mark: accept? (yes/no)

features.description: In the shared core, active only under failLoud: (1) first unencodable chunk (encodeStreamChunk returns nil) records nothing, delivers nothing, and latches non-retryable AIError{code:Internal, message:'unencodable stream chunk at provider index N; recorded log is an incomplete prefix'} - the prefix 'unencodable stream chunk' is PUBLIC CONTRACT and lives in a named constant; (2) the latched error cannot be overwritten by a later provider terminal success/error; (3) drain mode after the latch does no encode/record/deliver, only advances post-failure chunk count and post-failure payload bytes (no retention); (4) named constants recordedDrainMaxChunks = 256 and recordedDrainMaxBytes = 1 << 20, whichever exhausts first sets drainExhausted; (5) ON EXHAUSTION THE DRAIN GOES INERT - the callback's first statement is `if drainExhausted { return }`, counters saturate, NO PANIC, NO RECOVER, NO SENTINEL (see planner_ruling_sentinel); (6) counters provider_chunks (a floor once drain_exhausted) and delivered_chunks (== len(recorded) always), plus drain_exhausted:true in trace metadata; no skipped_chunks success path. OUT OF SCOPE: any change to aiStepWithStream's shipped silent skip (internal/effects/ai_step.go:377-382).

features.risk_note_row_13: The design doc's 'no dedicated bytecode op is needed' is CORROBORATED BUT NOT PROVEN for the new nested return. The controller confirmed runtime.CallEntrypoint is the evaluator-only dispatch path (cmd/ailang/run_helpers.go:473-483) and that both ops register via RegisterEffectBuiltin -> effects.Call -> RegisterOp('AI', ...), but nobody has tested eval<->bytecode value conversion for {chunks: [StreamChunk], outcome: Result[...]}. IF ROW 13 FAILS THAT IS A REAL FINDING, NOT A TEST BUG - stop and report it, do not paper over it. --strict-bytecode behaviour must stay identical to the existing callback-bearing stream function.

features.description: Merge-blocking contract text, moved up from the design doc's M3. (1) Builtin LongDesc for stepWithStreamRecorded MUST state all four: linear unbounded retention until the call returns; the log is exact w.r.t. chunks the provider ADAPTER EMITS not the wire (tool-call input_json stream content is never emitted as chunks by design, internal/ai/anthropic/streamstep.go:336-337); an unencodable chunk terminates the op with typed Internal (stable prefix 'unencodable stream chunk') and an explicitly incomplete prefix, after which AILANG records/encodes/delivers nothing and per-chunk work is bounded BUT THE CALL STILL RETURNS ONLY WHEN THE PROVIDER'S STREAM ENDS; and the deliberate divergence from stepWithStream, which silently skips an unencodable chunk (siblings equivalent only for fully-encodable streams, i.e. every stream constructible today). (2) Metadata Since: 'prototype' -> Since: 'v0.32.0', keep StabilityExperimental. (3) CHANGELOG.md entry under v0.32.0 unreleased crediting @arniwesth and linking #546 + arniwesth/ailang#2; do NOT touch the historical changelog 'open row' occurrence. (4) File the follow-up issue 'cancellable provider context across the AI surface (AIHandler v2)' - the honest fix for the wall-clock residual and the standing answer to R2's gpt5-6-sol objection; link from #546; do NOT start it. (5) Ask @arniwesth on #546 whether he prefers a first-class AIError code (IncompleteStream) over the stable message prefix - do not assume the answer.

human_question.text: The sentinel-panic abort is dropped, so the drain budget now bounds post-failure WORK (O(1)/chunk, zero retention) but NOT post-failure WALL-CLOCK - the call returns when the provider's stream ends. This is on a path unreachable for any StreamChunk constructible today. Accept?
human_question.if_no: The only remaining mechanism is a cancellable provider context - Mark's already-rejected option (b) - which becomes a blocking dependency and makes this a multi-sprint item.
